headline: 19 dead in Kolkata Durga Puja stampede; CM announces Rs 2.5 lakh compensation, PM Modi offers aid
summary: A stampede at a Durga Puja pandal in North Kolkata claimed 19 lives and injured 25 after an exit gate structure collapsed. West Bengal CM and PM Modi have announced compensation for the victims.
details: At least 19 people died in a stampede at the Chorbagan Sarbojonin community Durga Puja pandal on Muktarambabu Street in West Bengal’s North Kolkata. 17 of the victims died on the spot, and 25 others were injured, with one remaining in critical condition.

The tragic incident occurred on Saturday after a portion of the exit gate structure collapsed, leading to tension and a surge among visitors. This collapse triggered the stampede during the crowded Durga Puja festivities.

West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari announced Rs 2.5 lakh compensation and a job for each family that lost a member. The government will also cover 100% of medical expenses for all injured persons, alongside an additional Rs 5 lakh in compensation for them.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed his condolences and announced an ex-gratia of Rs 2 lakh from the PMNRF for the next of kin of each deceased. The injured will receive Rs 50,000 from the same fund, with the Prime Minister wishing them a speedy recovery.

CM Adhikari urged caution across the 58,000 Pujas in the state, emphasizing the need for strict crowd control measures. He stressed full adherence to fire brigade and police directives regarding adequate lighting, entry-exit points, and overall safety protocols.

headline: BNP leader alleges 'laptops eaten up' by party insiders, questions fertilizer dealership in Joypurhat
summary: A Facebook post by BNP National Executive Committee member Faisal Alim, alleging irregularities in laptop distribution and fertilizer dealership in Joypurhat, has ignited significant debate within the party and on social media.
details: Faisal Alim, a member of the BNP National Executive Committee, posted on Facebook alleging irregularities in the free distribution of laptops among 'July fighters' and the allocation of fertilizer dealerships in Joypurhat. He claimed party workers were deprived, sparking widespread discussion on social media and within the party.

In his post, Alim wrote, 'The laptops were divided and eaten among themselves,' metaphorically suggesting misappropriation. He further claimed that 20 to 30 percent of the 'eating' was completed in the last six months, and now that 'nothing is left,' the 'eating' has been suspended. He also questioned the fertilizer dealership allocations, alleging that relatives were favored, leaving 'oppressed' party workers without opportunities.

The Facebook post drew varied reactions in the comments section. While some criticized Faisal Alim, others brought forth new allegations. One commenter, Tariq Hossain Khan, hinted at financial transactions in local election nominations, stating, 'More eating is yet to come. Now members and chairmen are being sold; they are saying, come everyone, give money, take a ticket.'

Conversely, some commenters criticized Alim himself. Belal Hossain suggested Alim, as a central leader, should focus on his own responsibilities, describing his posts as 'cheap' and 'for show.' Another, Zillur Rahman, compared Alim's post to Jamaat's propaganda, claiming it benefits Jamaat and that Alim's 'hatred' led to the defeat of a BNP candidate.

When contacted, Faisal Alim defended his stance, stating, 'The people of Joypurhat know who divided the laptops and the percentages involved in various projects. The truth must be told.' Regarding fertilizer dealerships, he added, 'It has been revealed who received the fertilizer dealerships recently. Some took it in their mother-in-law's name, some in their brother-in-law's name. Was there a shortage of party workers? Why didn't they get it?'

Alim clarified that his post was not against the party but in its favor, aligning with the party chairman Tarique Rahman's stance against corruption. However, he did not provide specific details, individuals, projects, or documents to substantiate his allegations regarding laptop distribution, alleged project percentages, or favoritism in fertilizer dealerships.
Joypurhat District BNP Convener Golzar Hossain told Prothom Alo, 'I have seen Faisal Alim's Facebook status. It offended my sensibilities. Yet, the person who posted it felt nothing.'
